archetype.name: Playoff Team (possession-first)
archetype.definition: A team that shoots below the league but wins the possession game, protecting the ball, forcing turnovers and crashing the offensive glass, behind a top-five defense it also had last year.

report.headline: Toronto wins the possession battle; the shooting and the blowout-padded margin need watching.
report.take:
Toronto at 3-3 looks like a coin flip, but the profile underneath is more interesting. The Raptors rank 7th in Net Rtg at 7.6, with the 9th offense and the 5th defense. They get there almost entirely by having more chances than the other team. They are 1st in Opp TOV % at 18.9 and 3rd in TOV % at 11.8, and their ORB % of 32.6 ranks 2nd. The shooting, meanwhile, is poor: eFG % of 51 ranks 22nd, 3P % of 32 ranks 24th, and they take fewer threes than almost anyone. This team beats you on shot volume, not shot quality.

The defense tells the same story. A 108.2 DRtg ranks 5th, the same Def Rank as last season, but the shot defense is ordinary. Opponents post a 53.4 Opp eFG % (16th) and hit 36.7% from three (21st), and Toronto lets them get to the rim more often than the league does. Strip out the turnovers and this is a middling defense. The steals and deflections are carrying it, and an 18.9 forced-turnover rate sits well above anything in the last five seasons of history.

The point differential flatters them too. The 47-point margin rests on two routs, 135-92 over Chicago and 129-99 over Orlando. Over the last five games Toronto is 2-3 with a differential of just 0.8 a game, and it has allowed 121 and 131 in the last two losses. The W vs Pt Diff of -1 says they've been a bit unlucky, but the margin they've been unlucky against is inflated. The roster adds questions of its own. Kawhi Leonard, 8th on the SF tab, has played only 2 games on 46.6 TS %. Scottie Barnes is carrying a 33 USG % on 52.6 TS % with a -7.8 On-Off. Jamal Shead's minutes come with a -21 On-Off.

The upside is real, though. Last year this core shot a 54.6 eFG % and 35.4% from three, so some of the shooting drought should lift. Ball security has been a Raptors trait for years. If the shooting recovers even as the turnover and offensive-rebound edges regress, the net result is roughly the solid playoff-level team of last season, not the 7th-best team the early rating suggests.

strengths.title: Winning the turnover battle both ways
strengths.body: Toronto leads the league in Opp TOV % and ranks 3rd in TOV %, which hands it extra possessions every night. The ball security is a long-standing trait: the TOV % sat between 10.3 and 13.3 across the history. The forced-turnover rate is far above any prior season, so expect it to come down, though not all the way.

strengths.title: Second chances on the offensive glass
strengths.body: An ORB % of 32.6 ranks 2nd and sits well above the league average. It's how a below-average shooting team still scores at a 9th-ranked rate. Last year's ORB % was 25.5, so this is new and likely partly a small-sample spike.

strengths.title: A top-five defense, again
strengths.body: The 108.2 DRtg ranks 5th, matching last season's Def Rank. That continuity suggests the defensive identity is real. It leans on turnovers rather than contesting shots, though.

concerns.title: Shooting well below the league
concerns.body: Toronto's eFG % of 51 ranks 22nd, its 3P % of 32 ranks 24th, and it rarely shoots threes. Last year the eFG % was 54.6, so part of this is a cold start that should warm up. The low three-point volume, though, is structural.

concerns.title: Margin built on two routs
concerns.body: The season differential looks strong, but it rests on the blowouts of Chicago and Orlando. Over the last five games the differential is nearly even and the defense has leaked points. Read the 7.6 Net Rtg as a ceiling for now, not the baseline.

concerns.title: Shot defense is only average
concerns.body: Under the turnovers, opponents shoot a league-average eFG %, hit threes at a 21st-ranked clip and get to the rim often. If the forced turnovers regress, this defense drifts toward the middle of the league.

trend.note: Toronto opened with big home wins and has since swung between routs and losses, dropping the last two while allowing 121 and 131. The early margin is cooling toward even.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, two soft, then unbeaten Memphis at home
weekAhead.body:
The trip opens with the best spot of the week. The Clippers sit 27th on the site and have the league's worst TOV % at 18.4, which plays straight into Toronto's league-best ball-hawking. Milwaukee also looks winnable: its DRtg of 122.1 ranks 28th, and it forces the fewest turnovers in the league, so Toronto's possession edge should hold there. The Bucks do rebound well, at 49 a game, which could blunt the offensive glass.

Denver in the middle is a coin flip. The Nuggets' 21st-ranked defense and weak DRB % give Toronto openings, but they shoot well and have an A+ backcourt. The week ends at home against Memphis, 6-0 and 1st on the site, with the 2nd-ranked offense and defense and the league's best 3P %. That is a bad fit for a team that lets opponents shoot. Two wins is the floor to expect and three is realistic.

keyMatchups.title: Turnover hunters vs careless Clippers
keyMatchups.body: Toronto leads the league in forcing turnovers, and the Clippers are last in protecting the ball. This is where the possession edge should be widest. One caution: Clippers opponents' SGs have feasted, so expect Walter's minutes to matter.

keyMatchups.title: Barrett and Barnes find soft spots
keyMatchups.body: Denver ranks near the bottom in points allowed to small forwards, and Milwaukee is similarly generous to power forwards. Those are the slots where Barrett and Barnes carry the scoring load. Efficient nights from them would ease the shooting problem.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis shooting vs leaky perimeter
keyMatchups.body: Memphis shoots a league-best 3P % and runs a 15.1 Net Rtg. Toronto allows opponents a 21st-ranked 3P %, so the Raptors will need a big turnover margin to keep pace.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the forced-turnover rate holds up against Denver and Memphis, two teams that don't simply give the ball away.

restOfSeason.body:
The likely path is a solid playoff-level team close to last season's 46-36, not the 7th-ranked juggernaut of the early Net Rtg. Two things should come back to earth: the league-best forced-turnover rate and the offensive rebounding, both well above anything in recent history. The shooting should recover toward last year's levels, which offsets part of that. The current pace of 41 wins understates the team somewhat, and the margin overstates it. A range of 40 to 47 wins with a Net Rtg of 1.5 to 4.5 captures it.

Two variables move the ceiling most. The first is Leonard: 2 games is too few to judge, and if he settles in alongside Barnes, that changes the shot-creation problem. The second is whether Barnes can carry a 33 USG % more efficiently. The floor depends on whether the turnover-driven defense still holds when opponents protect the ball.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting returning to last year's level
How far the forced-turnover rate regresses

confidence.note: Six games, two of them blowouts; the ratings will move a lot.
